text: Although a majority of research on the ketogenic diet has been carried out in sedentary individuals, emerging data are beginning to shed light on the longitudinal effects of low-carbohydrate versus carbohydrate-rich diets on resistance training-induced hypertrophic adaptations. Early research in overweight, untrained women showed that adoption of a ketogenic diet combined with resistance exercise did not increase lean mass after 10 weeks, whereas a control group following their usual and customary diet achieved an increase of 1.6 kg (3.5 lb) of lean mass (60).
